The designed control strategy for the small-world HR neural networks incorporates a self-adjusting mechanism for control gains, eliminating the necessity for former gain selection. These gains decrease over time and converge to zero once synchronisation is achieved, ensuring that control effort is minimised and improved efficiency. Here, the small-world memristive HR neural networks depict various discharge oscillations and chaotic behaviour under external current stimulus conditions. The proposed bi-HR memristive coupled network addresses the stochastic spiking and realistic scenarios of neural activity under the environment of RNN. It also exhibits self-boosting of attractors, governed by synaptic parameters.

title: Set-reset latch operation in a bistable FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron driven by correlated additive and multiplicative noise
abstract: Nonlinear systems can harness noise to enhance the reliability of logical operations—a phenomenon known as logical stochastic resonance (LSR). In a bistable FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron, both additive and multiplicative noises individually induce LSR, enabling robust Set-Reset latch operation. For each noise type, the success probability P exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on noise intensity, with an optimal window yielding perfect latch performance. When both noises are present and uncorrelated, they act synergistically, creating a broad region of high reliability in the parameter plane. The most striking result concerns noise correlation: depending on baseline intensities, strong positive correlation can either severely degrade or dramatically improve latch performance. Heatmaps reveal that as correlation strength increases, the high-reliability region shifts and narrows; at perfect positive correlation, it splits into two lobes away from the diagonal. We further adopted a unified theoretical framework centering on effective noise intensity, explaining all numerical features—LSR peaks, inverse P trends against noise correlation strength, and lobe-split heatmaps. These findings demonstrate that a single FHN neuron can serve as a memory element enabled by noise, and that noise correlation significantly modulates the latch reliability, highlighting its importance for noise-assisted information processing.

title: Design, modelling, testing and application of hydraulic suspension components for rail vehicles: a state-of-the-art review
abstract: Rail transport is a safe, efficient and ecological way to meet the growing demand for a more connected and developed society. In the last decades, the development of passenger rail vehicles with improved ride quality and higher commercial speed have been supported by the research and optimization of new suspension components. Hydraulic suspension components (HSCs) represent a significant share of the most recent innovations proposed in this context. This paper provides a state-of-the-art review of the design, modelling, testing and application of HSCs, also discussing the effect of degradation and failure in these components. The paper aims to highlight the most recent advancements in these fields and the emerging trends that will likely be addressed in the near future to further support the development of new rail vehicles.

title: Nonlinear Interaction of Material Gradation and Electromagnetic Excitation in Rotating Shafts
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the nonlinear dynamic behavior of rotating shafts made from functionally graded materials (FGMs) under oscillating electromagnetic excitation. The primary goal is to understand the resonant response, governed by geometric nonlinearity and influenced by material inhomogeneity and the inertial nonlinearity of high-speed rotation. Methods The nonlinear governing partial differential equations were discretized into ordinary differential equations using the Galerkin method. The method of multiple scales was then employed to derive approximate analytical solutions for the system’s response, focusing on primary and combination resonances. Results Frequency-response relationships were obtained, revealing complex nonlinear phenomena. A detailed parametric analysis demonstrated high sensitivity to the material gradation profile, magnetic field characteristics, and excitation parameters. Numerical simulations captured the emergence and disappearance of double-jump hysteresis and the occurrence of Hopf bifurcations. Conclusion This analysis confirms that the dynamic stability and resonant response of FGM rotating shafts can be effectively tuned through material composition and electromagnetic field control. The identified nonlinear phenomena, such as bifurcations and jump behavior, are critical for the design and safe operation of high-speed rotating machinery. The presented analytical framework provides a valuable foundation for predicting and controlling the dynamics of such advanced systems.

title: Experimental and Numerical Studies on Dynamic Response and Fracture Characteristic of Sandstone with Multiple Defects
abstract: Geological discontinuity effect on fracture and seismic isolation under confinement and impact loading. Holes induce radial cracks and arching, while flaw tips drive stress concentration and directionality. Vortex-like velocity fields and anisotropic contact force link mesoscopic crack into macroscopic fracture. Complex discontinuities weaken energy storage capacity and enhance frictional dissipation, raising failure risks. Geological discontinuities (e.g., cracks, joints, faults, and cavities) fundamentally alter the integrity and mechanical behavior of rock masses. Under dynamic loading, such discontinuities induce stress concentration, disturb stress-wave propagation, and govern crack evolution, thereby acting as critical triggers for dynamic hazards in underground engineering. This study systematically investigates the dynamic response of sandstone containing multiple interacting defects, including intact, hole, flaw, intersected hole–flaw, and independent hole–flaw configurations. A combined experimental–numerical approach is employed, integrating triaxial Hopkinson bar (Tri-HB) expriment with quantitatively validated continuum-discrete coupling simulation. The results show that distinct dynamic stress–strain responses and fracture characteristics are governed by multiple interacting defects. Holes predominantly induce radial cracks and arching effects, while flaw tips cause strong directional stress concentration, with the inclination angle controlling crack propagation and seismic isolation. Hole–flaw intersected structures significantly accelerate crack coalescence, whereas hole–flaw independent structures exhibit pronounced energy dissipation and seismic isolation. At the mesoscale, failure evolution follows a sequence: shear triggering, tensile propagation, global instability. Force chain disturbance governs crack initiation direction, and local vortex-like velocity fields emerge near discontinuity intersections, promoting crack connectivity and dynamic instability. Energy partitioning analysis demonstrates that linear strain energy remains the dominant storage pathway, while complex discontinuities weaken storage capacity and markedly enhance frictional sliding, damping dissipation, and fragment motion, thereby enhancing energy dissipation and reducing energy storage capacity. These findings offer theoretical insights into the dynamic failure mechanisms of rock masses containing multiple discontinuities and guidance for hazard prevention in underground engineering.

title: Hybrid Mathematical Modelling and Embedded Learning for Semi-Active Friction Damping in Non-Smooth Vibration Control
abstract: Purpose This study establishes a mechanics-first, dimensionless and uncertainty-aware benchmark for bounded normal-load semi-active friction damping. It evaluates admissible normal-load modulation through a reproducible mechanics framework rather than presenting reinforcement learning as an isolated controller. Methods A two-degree-of-freedom oscillator is coupled to a regularised Stribeck friction law and a first-order normal-load actuator. Constant-load baselines, skyhook logic, Clipped-LQR control and TD3-RL command replay are evaluated under identical plant, actuator and metric definitions. The evidence comprises 72 settings and 345 controller-case evaluations, including 24 excitation-frequency ratios, six actuator-bandwidth settings, five normal-load-authority settings, 30 matched Monte Carlo realisations and six Euler/RK4 replay treatments. Results In the fixed episode, TD3-RL reduced RMS displacement by 2.9% and increased friction work by 28.4% relative to effort-matched Const_avg. Relative to Const_max, it used 31.8% less mean normal load and reduced RMS acceleration by 20.2%, with a 1.1% displacement penalty. Across 30 matched realisations, TD3-RL and Const_avg each produced lower RMS displacement in 15 cases, whereas TD3-RL produced lower RMS acceleration than Const_max in 29. Across 24 frequency ratios, the displacement-minimising strategy changed among all five deterministic baselines. Conclusion Normal-load timing can increase frictional dissipation without increasing average clamping, but the displacement benefit is operating-regime dependent. Semi-active friction damping should therefore be assessed jointly through displacement, acceleration, load exposure and uncertainty rather than through a single attenuation metric. The evidence is simulation-based; calibrated hardware validation remains necessary.

title: Adaptive event-triggered dual hybrid non-fragile control for USV–PLL time-delay systems with unmatched disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive event-triggered dual hybrid non-fragile control architecture designed to address severe complex time-delays and unmatched disturbances inherent in unmanned surface vehicle (USV) and phase-locked loop (PLL) coupled systems. A unified continuous-time affine nonlinear time-delay system model is first constructed, which explicitly quantifies the profound coupling relationship between USV macroscopic mobility and PLL microscopic phase errors. Secondly, a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) online adaptive approximation of unmodeled USV hydrodynamic nonlinearities is introduced, reducing the conservatism of global Lipschitz conditions. Additionally, a dynamic event triggering mechanism (DETM) with adaptive thresholds is designed to optimize limited communication bandwidth while theoretically preventing the Zeno phenomenon. To further enhance system resilience, the single perturbation assumption is broken by constructing a dual hybrid non-fragile parameter perturbation matrix for the feedback controller and interference observer. Unmatched interference is projected into a feasible finite thrust space via a pseudo-inverse matrix for active compensation. Through Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional analysis, the highly nonlinear coupled parameter problem induced by time-delays is transformed into standard linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Rigorous theoretical proofs and comparative simulations demonstrate that the closed-loop USV–PLL system achieves globally uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB) stability and satisfies the prescribed finite time-domain $$\mathcal {H}_{\infty }$$ H ∞ robust suppression level.

title: Experimental study on freezing-dynamic deterioration damage characteristics of joint-filled rock samples of cold regional open-pit slope
venue: Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment
abstract: Research on instability and disaster control of high-altitude alpine open-pit slopes is a core issue in geotechnical slope engineering. Based on a high slope project of a cold-region open pit in Xinjiang, China, this paper conducted theoretical analysis, laboratory rock mechanics tests and synchronous acoustic emission (AE) characteristic tests to investigate the damage deterioration characteristics of joint-filled rock samples with different joint inclination angles (0°, 25°, 50°, 75°) under the combined effect of freeze–thaw cycles and cyclic loading and unloading. The Gaussian mixture model was adopted to reveal the failure modes, crack distribution and evolutionary characteristics of rock samples. The results showed that freeze–thaw action accelerated the expansion of pore cracks inside rock samples and significantly deteriorated their mechanical properties, which mainly manifested as the decreases in the compressive strength and elastic modulus; axial strain, radial strain and Poisson’s ratio presented different variation trends with joint inclination angle and freeze–thaw damage degree. Under the coupling of freeze–thaw cycles and cyclic loading and unloading, rock specimens with larger joint inclinations showed superior anti-fatigue performance, while those with smaller joint angles experienced severe strength and stiffness attenuation. For instance, the strength and stiffness of the 25° joint-filled specimen decreased by 47.18% and 36.65%, respectively, while the 75° specimen had the minimum loss and withstood 13.5 cyclic loading levels. Obvious AE responses with Kaiser and Felicity effects existed in each loading stage, and rock specimens with larger joint inclination angles were more prone to shear failure.

title: A Perovskite Memdiode-Based Neuromorphic in Silico Surrogate Model for Emulating Predictive Coding Failure in Diabetic Neuropathy
abstract: Halide perovskite memdiodes have coupled ionic-electronic dynamics and are promising candidates for artificial synapses in neuromorphic computing. We provide an in silico neuromorphic circuit that includes a comprehensive perovskite memdiode model and confirm its synaptic plasticity repertoire through simulation-based validation. The proposed model recapitulates analog long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD), spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), spike-rate-dependent plasticity (SRDP), and paired-pulse facilitation/depression (PPF/PPD). We also describe pulse-amplitude- and pulse-width-dependent conductance modulation, pinched hysteresis I-V curves, and statistical robustness to device-to-device and cycle-to-cycle fluctuations through Monte Carlo simulation. This memdiode is implemented into a continuous-time neuromorphic predictive coding framework to minimize Variational Free Energy (VFE). In this architecture, we directly map four clinical hallmarks of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN)—plasticity impairment, homeostatic failure, afferent attenuation, and conduction delay—to localized circuit parameters ( $$\:k_{drift},\tau_{TH},A_{amp},\tau_{delay}$$ ). One severity parameter α is used to continuously tune the network between healthy predictive coding and computational collapse. Healthy baseline parameters minimize VFE quickly. Moderate DPN (α = 0.5) results in permanently elevated oscillatory VFE, a hypothetical counterpart of allodynia. Severe DPN (α ≥ 0.8) paralyzes the homeostatic plasticity, and the system collapses to a frozen maladaptive state that is similar to sensory ataxia. The noise resilience analysis and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis indicate that the architecture is highly resilient to stochasticity within the simulated parameter space and structurally robust to hyperparameter perturbations in all dynamical regimes. The primary contribution of this work is a computational framework demonstrating how second-order, BCM-capable memristive device dynamics can be used to model systems-level predictive-coding failure; the behaviorally validated perovskite memdiode model and the DPN severity mapping serve as a concrete, illustrative instantiation of this framework.

title: Communicative Action in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Theorizing LLMs as Communicative and Strategic Agents
abstract: The emergence of LLMs necessitates a re-evaluation of communicative agency in social systems. Integrating Habermas’s theory of communicative action with speech act theory, this paper investigates whether LLMs can engage in communicative action, produce speech acts, and function as social agents. We advance the novel claim that LLMs are “asymmetrical communicative agents” that satisfy behavioral but not intentional conditions for communicative action. While LLMs cannot yet generate genuine illocutionary acts, they produce significant perlocutionary effects. We adopt a gradualist position, arguing that LLMs lack a full-fledged “cognitive-volitional” complex, making them susceptible to co-option for strategic action even as they intervene in canonical communicative scenarios. This dual-status ontology suggests LLMs are quasi-social agents capable of advancing validity claims and influencing social norms. After anchoring LLMs within a “digital lifeworld,” we analyze their evolving roles across the strategic-communicative spectrum and their implications for the construction of social reality.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Symbolic Regression: State-of-the-Art Approaches, Key Applications, Benchmark Evaluations, and Future Research Directions
venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
abstract: Symbolic regression autonomously discovers interpretable mathematical expressions from data by optimizing functional structure and associated parameters. Unlike traditional regression approaches that rely on predefined model forms, symbolic regression generates explicit models that maintain high predictive accuracy while providing valuable scientific insights. This survey comprehensively analyzes contemporary symbolic regression methodologies by systematically integrating four paradigmatic approaches: deterministic methods, metaheuristic algorithms, neural-symbolic frameworks, and emerging hybrid strategies. We establish a unified taxonomic framework that bridges evolutionary computation, mathematical programming, and deep learning paradigms. Our analysis reveals convergence patterns toward physics-informed discovery, multi-objective optimization, and human-collaborative frameworks. WWe examine hybrid integration strategies, semantic-aware operators, and constraint-handling mechanisms, and we critically assess evaluation methodologies, benchmarking practices, applications across scientific and engineering domains, and fundamental limitations, including search complexity, overfitting, and high-dimensional scaling challenges. This work makes four key contributions. First, we provide a unified framework analyzing over 300 methods across four paradigms. Second, we offer comprehensive coverage of developments from 2020 to 2025, including transformer-based and large language model approaches. Third, we present a systematic analysis of hybrid strategies and convergence patterns. Fourth, we provide actionable guidance for method selection. This survey establishes a comprehensive contemporary reference for symbolic regression research, highlighting pathways toward robust, interpretable, and scalable automated scientific discovery systems.

title: A hybrid state-aware chaotic particle swarm optimization scheme for sensor deployment in wireless sensor networks
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) support situational awareness, environmental surveillance, and intelligent infrastructure, with node deployment playing a decisive role in coverage performance and system resilience. Achieving broad area coverage under strict k -coverage constraints remains a challenging optimization problem. It is essential to prevent node clustering and node isolation during the deployment process. Conventional particle swarm optimization (PSO) often tends to stagnate in complex deployment spaces, yielding insufficient coverage and redundant placements. In this study, a hybrid state-aware chaotic PSO (HSA-C-PSO) framework is formulated for WSNs coverage optimization. Tent map perturbations are incorporated into velocity updates to strengthen the swarm’s ability to escape local optima, while a hybrid refinement mechanism—combining Gaussian mutation with localized neighborhood search—maintains population diversity and improves local exploitation. Coverage ratio, k -coverage deficit, and repulsive potential fields are integrated into a composite fitness model that regulates spatial distribution and mitigates redundancy. Evaluations on large-scale deployment scenarios show marked gains in overall coverage, spatial uniformity, and reduction of isolated or overcrowded nodes relative to existing chaotic PSO variants and advanced metaheuristics. The improved convergence speed and stability indicate strong potential for reliable WSNs deployment planning.

title: van der Waals Josephson junctions for quantum science and technology
abstract: Josephson junctions (JJs) made out of van der Waals (vdW) materials offer a unique route to explore novel functionalities in superconducting devices such as emergent phases, anisotropic order parameters and crystalline tunnel barriers that remain inaccessible in conventional JJs. Over the past decade, vdW JJs have advanced rapidly, driven by new fabrication techniques and a diverse vdW materials library that enables the integration of materials with vastly disparate properties for scientific exploration. Beyond material diversity, vdW crystalline materials offer new control over device symmetries, enabling the realization of Hamiltonians unique to 2D systems. Furthermore, the long relaxation times of excitations in 2D heterostructures open possibilities for creating quantum sensors, with the 2D material itself acting as an efficient bus for transmitting excitations to the active sensing element. The use of vdW materials has also opened up the opportunity to explore the effect of moiré structures and topology, which could lead to potential applications in quantum computation and ultra-sensitive hybrid sensors. Although opportunities abound with vdW JJs, the challenge of scalability must be surmounted for translation into real-world devices. In this Review, we synthesize current developments in this field and offer a forward-looking roadmap. van der Waals Josephson junctions offer opportunities to explore novel device functionalities in superconducting circuits. This Review discusses progress in different device architectures and provides a roadmap outlining near-term and long-term opportunities for the field.

title: State-of-the-art review of next-generation nanofluids: integrating geometry, composition, and artificial intelligence for smart heat transfer
venue: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry
abstract: To address the challenges of conventional coolants in high-performance thermal systems, nanofluids, which are suspensions of nanoscale particles in base fluids have emerged as an attractive alternative. Since their introduction in the late 1990s significant advances have been made in the understanding of how these fluids are improving heat transfer. However, there are still some problems that need to be addressed such as dispersion stability, long-term reliability, and the relationship between nanofluid composition and geometric design, which is not usually considered as a factor interacting together. The present review integrates geometry, composition, or material and machine learning (ML) as interacting design variables that affect performance of the nanofluid at the system level, in addition to the previous reviews focusing on geometry or composition separately. It focuses on the importance of standardized datasets for model generalization across various types of nanoparticles, base fluids and operating conditions, and the need for long-term stability testing under realistic operating conditions as a separate, under addressed requirement for reliable AI-based prediction. This review is compared with some very similar recent publications to show its particular contribution and to provide concrete directions for future research, thus connecting the laboratory-scale results to the industrial application scale. This review proposes that the best way to enable and implement the use of nanofluid technologies is to combine AI-driven optimization with system-level metrics such as heat transfer, pressure drop, entropy generation, and exergy efficiency. In high-consequence areas, like nuclear power, adoption will also rely on the certification and regulatory issues that have been discussed in more detail later in this review. This review concludes with an identification of the most important challenges and some specific research priorities for the field to move toward scalable, reliable, and sustainable nanofluid solutions in engineering practice. Graphical abstract

title: Bio-inspired decision making in robot swarms under biases
abstract: To operate autonomously, minimal robot swarms must make timely and reliable collective decisions despite noisy individual sensing and severe constraints on communication, computation, and memory. Achieving this capability could expand their use in applications such as healthcare, disaster response, and environmental monitoring. Here, we study how such swarms can rapidly and reliably reach consensus on the best among n discrete options by comparing two canonical mechanisms of opinion dynamics—direct-switch and cross-inhibition—simple yet effective rules for collective information processing observed in biological systems across scales, from neural populations to insect colonies. We generalise existing mean-field models by incorporating asocial biases that influence opinion dynamics. While swarms using direct-switch reliably select the best option in the absence of asocial dynamics, their performance deteriorates when such biases are introduced, often leading to decision deadlocks. In contrast, bio-inspired cross-inhibition enables faster, more cohesive, robust, and scalable decisions across a wide range of biased conditions. Our findings provide theoretical and practical insights into the coordination of minimal swarms, with implications for a broad class of decentralised decision-making systems across biology and engineering. thanks Motoaki Hiraga, and the other, anonymous, reviewers for their contribution to the peer review of this work.

title: A beneficial-predatory behavior-inspired sparrow search algorithm and its application in delayed fractional-order system controller optimization
venue: Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: For a class of single-input single-output fractional-order systems with time delay, this article presents a phase-compensated fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative controller, and develops a beneficial-predatory behavior-inspired sparrow search algorithm for parameter tuning. Specifically, a theoretical analysis of both time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics is conducted to qualitatively elucidate how the fractional order modulates their dynamic behaviors. Subsequently, the fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative controller is then augmented with a phase lead compensation network, forming a cascaded configuration that merges the tunability of fractional-order elements with the phase-advance characteristics of lead networks. Furthermore, a sparrow search algorithm inspired by beneficial-predatory behavior is introduced for intelligent parameter tuning. By integrating a dual-direction movement strategy, a diversity-based dynamic safety threshold mechanism, and a memory-based search mechanism, the population update rules are refined to prioritize risk avoidance for individuals in suboptimal regions. Using CEC 2022 benchmark functions, the beneficial-predatory behavior-inspired sparrow search algorithm is evaluated and compared with standard sparrow search algorithm, five classical algorithms, and four sparrow search algorithm variants. Ablation studies and Wilcoxon rank sum tests are further performed to verify the robustness of the proposed optimization algorithm. Eventually, the designed controller is tuned under four optimization criteria, and its application to fractional-order systems with large time-delay yields significantly enhanced transient response, reducing the overshoot by 41.27% and the settling time by 3.68% compared with the conventional fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative controller.

title: Dynamic Analysis of Two-Dimensional Piezoelectric Structures using the Enriched Finite Element Method
abstract: Purpose This study aims to improve the numerical accuracy of dynamic analysis for two-dimensional piezoelectric structures by developing an enriched finite element method (EFEM) within the conventional FEM framework. Methods Polynomial, trigonometric, and combined polynomial-trigonometric enrichment functions are introduced into the interpolation of both displacement and electric potential fields. The present formulations are validated using a benchmark piezoelectric transducer and further examined through free-vibration and harmonic-response analyses of piezoelectric structures. Results Under the same mesh discretization, the present EFEMs achieve substantially higher accuracy in free-vibration analysis than conventional FEM, with EFEM-N11 giving the best frequency predictions. In terms of computational efficiency, EFEM-N11 maintains a clear accuracy advantage over conventional FEM at a comparable computational cost, whereas EFEM-N3 provides a favorable compromise between accuracy and computational expense. In harmonic-response analysis, the EFEMs accurately reproduce both displacement and induced electric potential responses over the considered frequency ranges. Conclusion The present EFEMs improve the accuracy of coupled electromechanical dynamic analysis while reducing the dependence on fine mesh discretization, offering a practical and effective approach for accurately predicting the dynamic behavior of piezoelectric structures.

title: Investigating the information content of multiple signals using joint recurrence quantification
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
abstract: In signal analysis, information content reflects the extent to which uncertainty is reduced and decision-making confidence is improved. Nevertheless, measuring information content from noisy time series with mathematical modelling remains challenging. In nonlinear time-series analysis, recurrence plots and their quantification analysis are increasingly used to study vibro-acoustic and oscillatory systems. Joint recurrence quantification analysis (JRQA) allows the computation of features based on the dynamics of multiple, potentially physically distinct, phase spaces. Here, a two-coupled model of analytical saline oscillators is used, which offers controllable coupling parameters and rich synchronisation behaviour. However, JRQA has not been used to analyse coupling direction and phase synchronisation in analytical saline oscillator models, nor has diagonal-wise joint recurrence-based power spectral entropy been explored for measuring common information content in signals. Our results show that the joint recurrence rate increases with the coupling strength parameter and synchronisation level, while the power spectral entropy, as a measure of information content, decreases in the noise-free case. Further, by progressively decreasing the signal-to-noise ratio from 20 dB to –20 dB through the addition of Gaussian white noise, the information content is increased. Our findings demonstrate that joint recurrence-based power spectral entropy can provide an effective measure of common information embedded in time-series data. By quantifying the shared recurrent dynamics between signals, joint recurrence quantification analysis may be useful for multi-sensor signal analysis, particularly when the objective is to identify weak dynamical signatures that are not clearly observable in individual sensors. This approach could improve decision-making confidence in the future by enabling the detection of micro-vibrations buried in noise using low-cost, off-the-shelf sensors.

title: Dynamic modeling and vibration characteristic analysis of a high contact ratio double-helical star gear transmission system with tooth broken fault
abstract: 多齿啮合特性使得高重合度齿轮箱中断齿故障导致的早期振动特征不易识别。 针对这一问题, 本文量化了高重合度人字星型齿轮传动系统中断齿故障引起的啮合刚度变化, 并研究了相应振动特征的演化规律。 首先, 采用解析-有限元方法, 分别计算太阳轮、 行星轮和齿圈发生断齿故障时的啮合刚度。 随后, 建立高重合度人字星型齿轮传动系统的刚柔耦合动力学模型, 并利用子结构模态综合法对系统进行降阶, 以提高动力学响应求解效率。 所提出的啮合刚度计算方法和动力学模型分别通过有限元分析和多体动力学仿真结果进行验证。 结果表明, 断齿故障会引起啮合刚度降低, 并在齿轮啮合频率及其谐波附近产生边频调制现象。 在相同断齿程度下, 太阳轮和齿圈断齿引起的刚度下降程度大于行星轮断齿。 此外, 当太阳轮、 行星轮和齿圈分别发生断齿故障时, 边频能量比和边频分布指数均随故障程度加重而增大。 研究结果可为高重合度齿轮箱断齿故障的早期识别和状态监测提供参考。 In high contact ratio gearboxes, incipient vibration features induced by tooth broken faults may be masked by multi-tooth meshing characteristics. To address this challenge, the stiffness reduction caused by tooth broken faults is quantitatively evaluated, and the corresponding vibration characteristic evolution is systematically investigated in the high contact ratio double-helical star gear transmission system (HCR-DHSGTS). When tooth broken faults are introduced separately into the sun gear, planet gear, and ring, an analytical-finite element method is employed to calculate the time-varying meshing stiffness. By incorporating the time-varying meshing stiffness, a rigid-flexible coupling dynamic model is established. The component mode synthesis method is then applied to enhance computational efficiency. The proposed stiffness calculation method is verified by finite element analysis, and the proposed dynamic model is verified against the multibody dynamics simulations in ADAMS software. The results indicate that under tooth broken fault conditions, a progressive stiffness reduction is observed, accompanied by modulation sidebands around the gear meshing frequency and its harmonics. Under the same fault severity, the stiffness reduction is found to be more pronounced for the sun gear and ring gear than for the planet gear. Furthermore, two indicators of sideband energy ratio and sideband level factor are proposed. Subsequent analyses reveal that both indicators monotonically increase with the severity for all fault locations considered in this paper. These findings provide theoretical support and quantitative guidance for early warning and condition monitoring of high contact ratio gearboxes.

title: Study of the Mechanical Properties and Failure Mechanism of Annular Coal Rock Based on Acoustic–Optic Combined Monitoring and GDEM Numerical Simulation
abstract: As hole size increases, the failure mode changes from vertical splitting to ‘+’ composite splitting. Acoustic signals shift from single bursts to multiple gradual events, showing damage evolves from concentrated to distributed GDEM simulations successfully reproduce crack growth and confirm the reliability of experimental results. A unified model is developed to predict instability and failure in materials with holes. Uniaxial compression tests were conducted on annular coal specimens with different inner-to-outer diameter ratios ρ to investigate the effects of pore size on damage evolution and failure mode transformation. Combined with acoustic emission (AE), digital image correlation (DIC), and GDEM numerical simulations, the mechanisms governing the evolution of cracks from initiation to penetration and their acousto-optic response characteristics were systematically studied. The results show that as ρ increases, the peak load decreases monotonically, and the failure mode gradually changes from vertical splitting to ‘  +  ’ composite splitting. DIC shows that the strain concentration area is consistent with the height of the crack initiation point, and the vertical band distribution evolves into a multi-directional ‘  +  ’ distribution. The AE response characteristics gradually change from a single-peak high-amplitude burst type to a multi-peak progressive type, indicating that the damage evolution mechanism changes from main crack concentration instability to decentralized multicrack coevolution. The GDEM simulation reproduces the proportional evolution law of the crack propagation path and crack type well. An equation for evaluating the critical aperture ratio of transverse crack initiation is derived, and an aperture coupling continuous damage evolution equation considering the geometric amplification effect is constructed. The stress–energy–damage theory criterion is formed, which provides a theoretical basis for evaluating the stability and warning of the failure of coal and rock masses with holes.

title: Dynamic Modeling and Performance Evaluation of Two-Directional And Ultra-Low Frequency Enhanced Elliptical Gauge-Inspired Piezoelectric Energy Harvester
abstract: Abstract The ultra-low frequency vibrations of wind turbines exhibit significant potential for energy harvesting and provide power for low-power sensors. However, limited energy conversion efficiency in the ultra-low frequency range remains a major challenge. For wind turbines, energy harvesters should also be able to harvest large-amplitude vibrations from two directions. Herein, this work proposes an enhanced elliptical gauge-inspired piezoelectric energy harvester (EEG-PEH) for harvesting two-directional and ultra-low frequency vibration energy. The device features a variable cross-section piezoelectric beam, two sliding magnets, and four fixed magnets. Magnetic repulsion exerts axial pressure on the piezoelectric beam, while the inertial force from the sliding magnet applies axial tension. These two forces work synergistically to impose dynamic alternating tension-compression loads on the piezoelectric beam. Additionally, the device concentrates and amplifies the axial load through the variable cross-section piezoelectric beam, thereby enhancing the energy harvesting efficiency. An electromechanical coupling model that accounts for geometric nonlinearities was established to investigate the dynamic characteristics and electrical output of a piezoelectric beam under asymmetric axial forces applied at both ends. Additionally, bifurcation diagrams were employed to investigate the effect of nonlinear magnetic forces on the dynamic behavior of the system. Testing of the EEG-PEH prototype showed that the theoretical model can capture the main response trends and primary dynamic features of the system under ultra-low frequency excitation. The proposed harvester can harvest energy more efficiently below 2 Hz, and its output power density is 27.9% higher than that of the matched rectangular-beam reference harvester under identical test conditions.

title: Distributed-Parameter Modeling of Embedded Clamped-Clamped Beam Energy Harvesters for Helicopter Transmission Shafts
abstract: Purpose Self-powered sensing inside a hollow helicopter transmission shaft is difficult because the cavity offers no stationary reference frame and the embedded oscillator is exposed to high centrifugal loads. An embedded clamped-clamped beam energy harvester is a promising solution, but the lumped-parameter models commonly used for its design cannot describe how the beam's three-dimensional geometry and the boundary axial preload affect the dynamic response. This paper proposes a distributed-parameter electromechanical model to overcome this limitation. Methods The Galerkin truncation method is used to discretize the continuum in the rotating reference frame, and the coupled governing equations are derived from the extended Hamilton’s principle. Results Experimental results obtained on a rotating test rig agree well with the model. The analysis then reveals a competition between centrifugal softening and geometric hardening, which drives a bistable evolution; the nonlinear stretching produced by large deformations broadens the effective frequency band and keeps the chaotic response within safe boundaries, preventing divergent instability. Based on the model, simple design guidelines are obtained: the beam width can be tuned to shift the resonance band efficiently, while the beam length, thickness, and axial preload control the excitation threshold and the output peak. Conclusion The proposed model and design rules provide a practical basis for the geometric and boundary design of energy harvesters that operate under extreme variable-speed conditions.

title: A Review of Emerging Image Encryption Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions: From Classical Cryptography to AI-Driven
venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
abstract: The rising growth of digital media forces digital images as a significant medium for information exchange, indicating the need for stronger security over open networks. However, conventional cryptographic algorithms designed to encode text data are not optimal when applied to images due to high redundancy, strong dependency of pixels, and big files. Although various algorithms are being researched in the domain of cryptography, further investigation is required to analyze the shift from deterministic ciphers to modern AI-based methods and evaluate new deep learning and biology-inspired encryption structures. This review examines current advances in encryption techniques used to secure image transfer over open networks. In particular, it presents an overview of six classes of image encoding algorithms: classical cryptography, chaos-based, biology-inspired schemes, deep learning, transformer-based and hybrid encryption solutions. The paper focuses on high-quality sources published in the last five years and assesses the strengths and limitations of their structures in terms of robustness, key security, and differential resistance. Additionally, the review discusses performance metrics, the balance between speed and complexity, and appropriate use cases for each technique, providing recommendations on possible changes to enhance encryption processes and optimize performance. Overall, the findings indicate that future development in image encryption should focus on time-efficient processing of image data and domain-specific methods. It suggests focusing on lightweight architectures (e.g., State Space Models) and implementing hybrid encryption based on classical ciphers combined with AI-driven feature extraction.

title: Minor-interference-driven nonuniform gear meshing: modeling and dynamic characterization
abstract: The effects of tooth modification and deviations on gear transmission are generally interpreted in terms of altered local contact characteristics and contact ratio. However, these factors may also introduce minor interference between meshing teeth, resulting in asynchronous contact phenomena that have received limited attention in gear dynamics. This study investigates the effects of this phenomenon via surface gap modeling and dynamic analysis. A discrete-surface representation extends the model to arbitrary gear geometries. Finite element analysis validates that tooth contact can show significant changes under interference caused by misalignment. A modified dynamic model incorporates pre-coupled meshing parameters and applies to both spur and bevel gears. Based on this model, the interference effect is isolated by comparing the nominal state with a forced synchronous condition. Results indicate that minor interference can smooth load transfer, reduce abrupt stiffness changes, and suppress high-frequency vibration. Importantly, this study shows that inter-tooth interference induced by profile adjustments can also play a crucial role in gear contact evolution and meshing stability, in addition to the effects of local contact geometry commonly considered in conventional analyses.

title: Back-Analysis of the Initial In-Situ Stress Field Using Iterative Generalized Ridge Regression (GRR) with Anisotropic Regularization: A Multi-Criteria Optimization Approach
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of the initial in-situ stress field of rock masses is paramount for the stability analysis of deep underground engineering, particularly in high geo-stress environments. However, the inherent correlation between gravitational and tectonic stresses frequently induces severe multicollinearity. This causes the standard Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) inversion to yield distorted solutions. These solutions are characterized by physically unreasonable magnitudes of regression coefficients for tectonic stress fields, physically inconsistent negative coefficients for compressive stress fields, and statistically insignificant regression coefficients for key tectonic stress fields. To address the distorted solutions, this study proposes a new inversion strategy based on iterative Generalized Ridge Regression (GRR). Unlike Standard Ridge Regression (SRR), which applies uniform isotropic shrinkage, the proposed GRR method employs anisotropic regularization. By assigning individual regularization parameters to distinct canonical coefficients of gravitational and tectonic stresses, the method adaptively suppresses noise-dominated components amplified by multicollinearity while preserving valid geomechanical signals. In addition, an optimized Hoerl-Kennard iterative procedure is established, incorporating a multi-criteria termination protocol. Application to the Banzhulin Tunnel demonstrates that this protocol identifies an optimal iteration step that simultaneously satisfies statistical criteria (e.g., p -values ≤ 0.05), ensures essential physical constraints (e.g., positive coefficients for compressive stress fields), and avoids the over-regularization associated with full numerical convergence. Comparative analysis reveals that the GRR framework reduces the Residual Mean Squared Error (Residual MSE) by 14.4% relative to SRR and mitigates predictive drift in deep extrapolation zones. This research provides a statistically reliable and physically consistent methodology for resolving ill-posed inverse problems arising from multicollinearity among gravitational and tectonic stresses. The inherent correlation among gravitational and tectonic stresses induces multicollinearity, rendering Ordinary Least Squares inversion unstable. Generalized Ridge Regression outperforms Standard Ridge Regression through anisotropic regularization, which addresses the unequal contributions of gravitational and tectonic stresses to multicollinearity. A multi-criteria termination protocol provides a statistically reliable and physically consistent the initial in-situ stress field of rock masses.

title: Review: advances in flexible dielectric elastomer smart materials-from electromechanical fundamentals to frontier applications
abstract: In recent years, dielectric elastomers (DEs) have been widely adopted for flexible artificial muscles, soft robotics, flexible electronics, and biomedicine due to their excellent electromechanical conversion, large electrostrain, high energy density, and great flexibility. To systematically clarify the 25-year research evolution of DE smart materials, this paper performs bibliometric and quantitative analysis on Scopus-indexed publications and visualizes the developmental trends of DE technologies. First, the fundamental properties and characteristics of flexible DE smart materials and their composites are systematically classified and summarized. Second, recent advances in DE-related theoretical research are comprehensively sorted out and elaborated. Third, based on the unique performance merits of DEs, the state-of-the-art applications of DE technology are reviewed across diverse fields, covering flexible artificial muscles and soft robotics, flexible electronics, energy devices, optical devices, and biomedical engineering. Finally, the key bottlenecks limiting the further development of DE technology are discussed based on the current research status. On this basis, a design philosophy for fully flexible integration of energy, actuation, sensing, and control (FEASCI) is proposed for DE smart devices. Ultimately, existing limitations and future developmental directions of DE technologies are concluded to provide innovative insights for subsequent research. Graphical abstract

title: Rigid-flexible-coupled Transient Vibration Characteristics of a Magnetic-levitation Disk-shaft Rotor with Rub-impact
abstract: Purpose Magnetic-levitation disk-shaft rotor systems constitute the core component of advanced high-speed turbomachinery operating frictionless during stable conditions. Insufficient magnetic load capacity may cause rub-impact between the rotor and auxiliary bearings. This rotor system exhibits rigid and flexible transient vibrations, yet its rigid-flexible-coupled vibration characteristics remain inadequately characterized. A lack exists for a quantification parameter or method to assess rigid-flexible-coupled vibration intensity. Methods This study established a rigid-flexible-coupled transient dynamic model of a magnetic-levitation disk-shaft rotor with rub-impact. Three distinct vibration forms emerge during acceleration: rigid, rigid-flexible coupled, and flexible vibration. To quantitatively assess rigid-flexible-coupled vibration strength, the novel rigid-flexible-coupled coefficient and its quantitative method were proposed and validated. Results and Conclusions Vibration analysis of the rotor undergoing rub-impact revealed that following magnetic bearing failure, auxiliary bearings suppress the escalating transient vibration, allowing the rotor to operate stably for a period before instability develops. Instability initiates as rigid vibration, progressing to divergence in flexible vibration. Controlling post-rub rigid vibrations can prevent rotor instability. Specifically, smaller contact stiffness, smaller friction coefficients, and large rubbing clearances mitigate instability triggered by rigid vibration. However, a larger rubbing clearance could aggravate the flexible vibration. To ensure minimized and stable rigid-flexible-coupled vibrations, an optimal rubbing clearance should be selected. The flexible vibration consumes rub-impact vibration energy. Under energy conservation, the rigid vibration energy is weakened, making the flexible rotor less susceptible to rub-impact instability.

title: Investigation of hunting instability suppression in high-speed EMUs with a secondary lateral inerter damper
abstract: During the operation of electric multiple units (EMUs), abnormal vibrations caused by hunting instability have become increasingly prominent. An eight-degree-of-freedom half-vehicle theoretical model equipped with an inerter–spring–damper (ISD) suspension was established to analyze the hunting modes and critical speeds of EMUs. Subsequently, a co-simulation model based on Simulink and SIMPACK was developed. Using the root-mean-square (RMS) values of the lateral accelerations of the carbody and bogie as the optimization objectives, particle swarm optimization (PSO) was employed to optimize the key parameters of the ISD suspension. The modal analysis results showed that, compared with the conventional spring–damper (SD) suspension, the ISD suspension effectively increased the damping ratio of the hunting mode and suppressed the development of high-frequency instability. With the ISD suspension, the critical speeds of the vehicle system under the primary and secondary hunting conditions increased by 18.37 and 39.49%, respectively. In addition, the ISD suspension significantly reduced the lateral accelerations of the vehicle, wheelset lateral displacement, and the Sperling ride index over the investigated speed range. These results indicate that the secondary lateral ISD suspension can significantly improve the lateral stability of high-speed EMUs.

title: Synchronization criteria for hybrid impulsive dynamical networks via comprehensive impulsive average gain
abstract: This paper investigates global exponential synchronization of complex dynamical networks subject to hybrid impulses. A novel concept, termed the comprehensive impulsive average gain (CIAG), is introduced to characterize the combined influence of impulsive gains and impulsive intervals. Within this framework, three classes of impulsive schemes, including fixed impulsive gains, fixed impulsive intervals, and their simultaneous variations, are treated in a unified manner. Both uniformly bounded and unbounded impulsive intervals are taken into account. By employing a Lyapunov-based approach, sufficient conditions are derived to guarantee global exponential synchronization of the considered networks. In particular, for the case of unbounded impulsive intervals, an extended result is established to ensure the applicability of the proposed framework. It is shown that the proposed criterion is less conservative than the method of average impulsive gain (AIG). Numerical examples on scale-free and small-world networks are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

title: Nonlinear vibration of bolted shaft-disk-shaft rotors with clearance fit
abstract: Bolted shaft-disk-shaft rotors (BSDSRs) are key components in rotating machinery. They are typically supported by rolling bearings, where clearance fit is employed between the pedestal and the bearing. However, the vibration mechanism of BSDSRs with this support is still not well understood. In this paper, the nonlinear dynamic model of BSDSRs is constructed based on the Kirchhoff plate theory and Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, accounting for the bolted joint, the clearance fit, and disk deformation effects. The nonlinear vibration response is analyzed by the Newmark- β method. The nonlinear dynamic characteristics of BSDSRs are analyzed under different rotational speeds, fit clearances, and unbalanced masses. Results show that the fit clearance introduces strong nonlinear behavior. The chaotic, quasi-periodic, and periodic motions appear alternately when rotational speed increases. At low rotational speeds, rub-impact within the fit clearance drives the system into chaos. At high rotational speeds, sub-synchronous vibration component induces quasi-periodic motions. As the fit clearance increases, high-order harmonics in the spectrum are gradually enhanced. Increasing unbalanced mass widens the range of rotational speed for periodic motion, but it also increases the vibration response. The results provide a basis for fault diagnosis, performance evaluation, and design optimization of rotor systems with clearance fit.

title: Time-Delay Dynamics and Semi-Analytical Method for Hybrid Vibration Absorber
abstract: Background Time-delay effects in a hybrid vibration absorber may induce complex nonlinear behaviors and degrade suppression performance due to phase mismatch, even causing instability. Understanding the modulation of fast/slow dynamics by time delay is essential for both theory and control. Goals This study comprehensively analyzes a time-delayed hybrid vibration absorber. Objectives include determining bifurcation conditions, characterizing strongly modulated responses via geometric analysis of the slow invariant manifold, and extending the time-domain minimum residual method (TMRM) to nonlinear time-delay systems for semi-analytical solutions of periodic and quasi-periodic responses. Methods The complex averaging method separates fast and slow dynamics to derive saddle-node and Hopf bifurcation conditions. Geometric analysis yields the slow invariant manifold and verifies conditions for strongly modulated responses. A time-delay term incorporated into TMRM generalizes the method to time-delayed nonlinear systems, and semi-analytical solutions are validated against theoretical results. Results Bifurcation conditions and manifold characteristics are determined. Time delay exerts a dual effect-inducing complex dynamics or enabling tunable reduction-by modulating periodic orbit evolution. Semi-analytical solutions agree well with theory. The extended TMRM is validated in the theoretical context, providing a reference for further analytical and experimental studies on time-delayed nonlinear systems.

title: Self-adaptive metamaterial plate enabling asymmetric wave propagation for crack detection
abstract: Wave-based structural health monitoring (WSHM) methods employing metamaterials have attracted significant attention from both industry and academia. However, leveraging metamaterials with asymmetric wave propagation to purify signals and improve modeling of elastic wave-damage interactions remains a challenge. In this work, we propose exploiting asymmetric flexural wave propagation to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of WSHM. This phenomenon is realized in a self-adaptive metamaterial plate, for which two designs are developed. In the first, asymmetric wave propagation is achieved by applying different control parameters depending on the wave propagation direction. Secondly, gradient control parameters are introduced to break structural symmetry, thereby enabling asymmetric wave propagation. As an application, we propose a novel WSHM method for crack detection in plates based on the designed self-adaptive metamaterial. Compared with conventional approaches, the proposed method generates a more ordered wave field with minimal interference, leading to higher efficiency and accuracy. This work not only introduces two strategies for designing self-adaptive metamaterial plates that realize asymmetric wave propagation, but also opens new avenues for advancing metamaterial-based WSHM technologies. 基于超材料波动调控特性的结构健康监测方法已受到工业界和学术界的广泛关注. 然而, 如何利用超材料的非对称传输特性有效过滤杂波信号并提升结构健康监测精度, 仍是一个具有挑战性的问题. 针对该问题, 本研究提出了一种基于自适应超材料板的弯曲波非对称传输方法, 可有效提高结构健康监测的准确性. 本研究中, 自适应超材料板的非对称传输主要通过两种方式实现: 第一种是根据波的传播方向施加不同的控制参数, 从而实现弯曲波的非对称传输; 第二种是通过引入梯度控制参数打破结构对称性, 进而实现弯曲波的非对称传输. 基于自适应超材料板中宽频、 高效的弯曲波非对称传输特性, 本研究提出了一种用于板结构裂纹检测的新型结构健康监测策略. 数值结果表明, 与传统方法相比, 本文所提出的结构健康监测策略具有更高的检测准确性.

title: Surfactant Replacement and Aerosolized Inhaler Therapies for Virus-Induced Respiratory Disorders: Mechanisms, Advances, and Clinical Perspectives
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive and multidisciplinary analysis of two principal therapeutic strategies for virus-associated respiratory disorders, namely surfactant replacement therapy (SRT) and inhaler-based pulmonary drug delivery. The study examines the physiological foundation of pulmonary surfactant, highlighting its dual role in reducing alveolar surface tension and modulating innate immune defense. While SRT is firmly established as a life-saving intervention for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), emerging evidence supports its broader potential in viral pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and surfactant-assisted drug and cell delivery. The review further explores advances in inhalation-based drug delivery systems, including pressurized metered-dose inhalers (pMDIs), dry powder inhalers (DPIs), nebulizers, and soft mist inhalers (SMIs). Emphasis is placed on aerosol particle dynamics, airway geometry, and deposition mechanisms governed by impaction, diffusion, and sedimentation. Experimental findings and computational approaches are discussed to illustrate how fluid mechanics and numerical modeling optimize regional lung deposition and device performance. Additionally, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into respiratory medicine is examined, underscoring their role in imaging diagnostics, exacerbation prediction, personalized therapy, and smart inhaler development. Collectively, this review demonstrates that the convergence of surfactant biology, advanced aerosol engineering, computational modeling, and AI-driven precision medicine represents a transformative pathway for improving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of infectious and chronic pulmonary diseases.

title: The HydroGym reinforcement learning platform for fluid dynamics
abstract: Effective control of fluid flows is critical across transportation, energy and medicine, where it can increase lift, reduce drag, enhance mixing and attenuate noise^ 1 – 3 . Yet fluids are notoriously difficult to control because they involve high-dimensional, nonlinear and multiscale dynamics that resist conventional approaches^ 4 – 6 . Reinforcement learning has driven remarkable progress in fields such as protein folding and complex games, which have shared benchmarks and standardized environments^ 7 – 10 . Fluid dynamics has lacked such infrastructure, so each controller is typically tuned to a single geometry and operating condition, making progress difficult to accumulate, transfer and compare^ 11 – 13 . Here we introduce HydroGym, a solver-independent reinforcement learning platform providing more than 60 validated, openly available flow control environments spanning from canonical laminar flows to complex turbulent flows, with systematic progression in the Reynolds number up to Re = 4 × 10^5, and Mach number variations in two and three dimensions. Across these environments, agents repeatedly discover robust control principles, including boundary layer manipulation, disruption of acoustic feedback and reorganization of turbulent wakes. Critically, we demonstrate a proof of concept for zero-shot transfer, in which agents that are trained exclusively in inexpensive surrogate environments are deployed to challenging real-world scenarios such as a three-dimensional wing section. We achieve a 38% reduction in local skin friction while reducing exploration costs by four orders of magnitude compared with direct on-wing optimization. As this transfer exploits shared near-wall physics, the breadth of generalization remains open, suggesting a new pathway for research toward policy generalization across computationally prohibitive simulation environments. By offering a common, extensible foundation for reproducible research, HydroGym moves flow control from isolated case studies toward a cohesive community effort. HydroGym offers over 60 standardized reinforcement-learning flow-control environments and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to a 3D wing, cutting local skin friction by 38% and exploration costs by four orders of magnitude.

title: Experimental modal analysis of nonlinear systems using force-controlled harmonic testing
abstract: This paper presents the Force-Controlled Testing-Harmonic Force Surface (FCT-HFS) framework, a novel approach for experimental modal analysis that identifies nonlinear modal models using standard force-controlled testing. Based on single nonlinear normal mode theory and quasi-linearisation in experimental analysis of nonlinear systems, the framework represents nonlinearities as response-amplitude-dependent modal parameters. The framework involves conducting a series of force-controlled frequency response tests to construct a three-dimensional HFS. By slicing this surface at constant response amplitude planes, quasi-linear frequency response functions (FRFs) are extracted, allowing the identification of amplitude-dependent modal parameters through established linear modal identification techniques. The proposed framework is validated through numerical simulations and experimental investigations of two benchmark structures: the length-modified Brake-Reuß beam and the Orion beam. It is observed that the accuracy of synthesised responses is highly sensitive to the density of forcing levels and to the interpolation techniques employed during both HFS construction and modal-parameter curve fitting. Numerical and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately captures the nonlinear modal model of nonlinear systems, provided that no unstable branch exists in the frequency response. Consequently, the framework is well-suited for weakly nonlinear systems and systems with strong nonlinear damping where a jump does not occur. The FCT-HFS framework eliminates the need to measure quasi-linear FRFs through response-controlled testing using specialised control systems, enabling the use of well-established force-controlled harmonic testing methods and equipment while still capturing the key benefits of the response-controlled nonlinear modal analysis approach when there is no unstable branch in the frequency response. Graphical abstract

title: Nonlinear dynamics of micro-scale floating mass transducer oscillator under electrical and mechanical excitation
abstract: In the paper, a small-sized system with a Floating Mass Transducer (FMT) was investigated. Such a device can be used for vibration excitation (FMT as a vibration actuator) or for energy recovery (FMT as an energy harvester). Both applications were tested during the research. The developed FMT model accounts for the existence of two induction coils, whose connection configuration affects the electromechanical coupling in the system. The main goal of the paper is to show that for large oscillations, the two selected FMT configurations exhibit significantly different dynamic behaviors, while CMFT and DMFT exhibit identical responses in the linear regime. Their behaviors diverge markedly under strong excitations: the CFMT undergoes an earlier transition to multi-harmonic and chaotic responses, whereas the DFMT maintains quasi-linear characteristics over a broader operating range. Moreover, the study distinguishes between the dynamical effects of electrical and mechanical excitation sources, showing that electrical actuation induces complex subharmonic and chaotic phenomena, while mechanical excitation leads predominantly to superharmonic responses. To capture these behaviors, a dedicated FFT-based characterization framework was developed, overcoming the limitations of conventional analytical tools in describing strong nonlinearities. Finally, by contrasting actuator and energy-harvesting regimes, this work uncovers subharmonic generation as a key mechanism differentiating their dynamics, providing new insights for FMT devices operating in nonlinear domains. The study is intended as a theoretical and signal-oriented investigation of nonlinear response mechanisms, rather than a device validation or performance optimization study.

title: Smart vibration control of structural-functional integrated SMA-composite systems: nonlinear dynamics, progress, and perspectives
abstract: In the aerospace context, advanced composite materials are subjected to severe broadband dynamic loads. NiTiNOL shape memory alloys (NiTi-SMA) and novel NiTi steel wire ropes (NiTi-ST) provide a smart pathway for nonlinear vibration suppression through superelastic hysteresis. This review systematically presents the progress and perspectives of nonlinear dynamics and smart vibration control in NiTi-SMA-composite coupled systems, mapping a comprehensive technical framework from material modeling, structural dynamics, reduced-order solutions, physical validation to future technological pathways. This review paper compiles advanced structural mechanics frameworks for various composite configurations. It includes nonlinear hysteretic constitutive models into multi-type structural governing equations, and assesses the theoretical benefits of Galerkin truncation and frequency-time dual-track analytical mechanisms to describe complex topologies, e.g., resonance peak deflection, multi-stability. Most importantly, it emphasizes the systematic physical capture and validation of strong nonlinear phenomena, highlighting key experimental demonstrations of the nonlinear vibration reduction potential of NiTi-SMA and NiTi-ST in composite structures. State of the art testing methodologies such as slow bidirectional sweeps and dwell control are studied for an accurate calibration of jump boundaries and multi-stable topological evolution. Cross-verification shows small discrepancies between theoretical and physical realities. In addition, the survey proposes the future development routes such as multiphysics coupling, active/semi-active controllable damping, and data-driven optimization, which can provide an important theoretical reference for the next-generation intelligent aerospace equipment.

title: Modeling and Numerical Analysis of a Fractional-Order Armature-Controlled DC Motor
venue: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology, Transactions of Electrical Engineering
abstract: In this study, a fractional-order mathematical model is developed to describe the dynamic behavior of an armature-controlled DC motor by incorporating memory-dependent effects inherent in its electrical and mechanical subsystems. The classical integer-order motor equations are generalized using Caputo fractional derivatives, allowing a more flexible and realistic representation of armature current, angular velocity, and rotor position dynamics. The resulting fractional model reduces to the conventional DC motor model as a special case when the fractional orders approach unity, thereby ensuring consistency and physical interpretability. Numerical simulations are carried out using the explicit Toufik–Atangana (TA) numerical scheme, and the obtained results are rigorously validated through comparison with the benchmark Adams–Bashforth–Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method. Time-domain responses and sensitivity analyses are conducted to investigate the influence of fractional orders on the transient and steady-state characteristics of the motor, revealing that reduced fractional orders introduce non-local damping that effectively suppresses transient overshoots. Comprehensive computational profiling confirms the theoretical convergence of the TA scheme, while demonstrating exceptional efficiency-executing up to 75% faster and natively consuming 43% less memory than the ABM method at high resolutions. Furthermore, parametric robustness testing verifies that the fractional-order framework maintains stable, bounded periodic behavior even under substantial uncertainties in critical physical parameters.Ultimately, the comparative study demonstrates that the fractional-order formulation provides a superior, highly robust framework for capturing complex damping and memory effects in electromechanical systems.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and analysis of functionally graded porous circular/annular plate supported by nonlinear elastic foundation
abstract: Addressing the current scarcity of research on the nonlinear dynamics of functionally graded porous (FGP) circular and annular plates, particularly regarding amplitude-frequency response characteristics, this paper develops a novel theoretical model to capture the nonlinear dynamic behavior of such plates featuring thickness-dependent pore distribution supported by nonlinear elastic foundation, and investigates the regulatory laws governing the resulting nonlinear dynamic responses of geometry-, porosity- and foundation-related parameters. Building upon the large deformation assumption and first-order shear deformation formulation, nonlinear dynamic equations are derived using energy methods, and a hybrid solution framework integrating the incremental harmonic balance method and the spectral element method is established. The validity and versatility of the proposed approach are rigorously proven via comparisons with finite element simulations, benchmark literature, and numerical solutions for both linear and nonlinear cases. Parametric studies reveal strong correlations between the amplitude-frequency and amplitude-time responses and the aforementioned design parameters, particularly with foundation parameters exerting complex regulatory effects. This study provides an efficient analytical pathway for examining the nonlinear dynamics of FGP circular/annular plates, and the identified parameter-response relationships offer preliminary recommendations for the design and performance tuning of such structural elements.

title: Synchronization-based sliding mode control of a nine-mode reduced-order model of the 2D Navier–Stokes equations
venue: International Journal of Dynamics and Control
abstract: This paper investigates the synchronization and control of a reduced-order representation of the two-dimensional (2D) Kolmogorov flow, a canonical fluid-flow model governed by the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations under periodic boundary conditions and sinusoidal external forcing. Using a spectral Fourier–Galerkin expansion, a nine-mode dynamical system is obtained that captures the principal dynamical transitions and nonlinear interactions observed across a wide range of Reynolds numbers. Within this framework, the study develops static and dynamic sliding-mode synchronization schemes designed to drive the trajectories of a slave (controlled) system toward those of a master (reference) system, thereby achieving synchronization of the reduced-order dynamics. Synchronization strategies are examined under two scenarios: when the Reynolds number is precisely known and when it is not known. In the latter case, an adaptive control law is introduced to estimate the unknown Reynolds number online. Numerical simulations are performed to evaluate the proposed synchronization strategies under various dynamical regimes. The results demonstrate that all four controllers achieve effective synchronization of the reduced-order systems under both known and unknown Reynolds numbers. Furthermore, the dynamic sliding mode controllers significantly reduce the chattering associated with conventional sliding mode control while preserving the synchronization accuracy.

title: Engineering Next-generation Drug Delivery Systems Via 4-D Printing: A Paradigm Shift Toward Precision Medicine
abstract: Four-dimensional (4-D) printed constructs have recently become clinically relevant platforms for customized and precise drug delivery due to their bio-programmability, bio-responsiveness, and spatiotemporal transformative potential. The 4-DP bio-constructs are highly bio-interactive and dynamically evolving as per therapeutic requisite. In this review, we aim to provide a detailed discourse on the key mechanisms that drive 4-D transformations of a broad spectrum of materials-ranging from shape-memory (SM) systems, liquid crystalline elastomers (LCEs), self-healing and multi-responsive polymers, metamaterials, and select bio-derived materials. The review also summarizes various conventional and advanced additive manufacturing strategies that have been employed for 4-DP of various bio-constructs. Contemporary representatives of various 4-DP drug delivery devices such as smart hydrogels and scaffolds, implants, stents, prosthetics, microneedles, responsive biomedical devices, and dynamic organ- and tumor-on-chip platforms have also been highlighted. Characterization methodologies, preclinical considerations, translational challenges, and the evolving patent and industrial landscape have also been recapitulated. The review also intends to provide critical perspectives on the expanding horizons and translational glitches of 4-DP while elucidating the key bottlenecks to its commercial large-scale integration and clinical translation. Graphical Abstract

title: Chamfer effect in the step and Eddy corner of the backward-facing step fluidic oscillator
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
abstract: A backward-facing step fluidic oscillator (BFSFO) was modified by creating chamfers at step and Eddy corners with variations from 20% to 80%. Analysis was conducted using CFD methods involving an SST k-ω turbulence model. Reynolds numbers ranged from 3 × 10⁴ to 5.5 × 10⁴. Results concluded that a 20% step corner chamfer model is highly optimal for active flow control devices, capable of producing significan frequency ( f ) (an average increase of 5.44%), reducing average pressure drop (ΔP_ave), and maintaining an optimal pressure fluctuation (PF). Conversely, a 20% Eddy corner chamfer configuration shows an excellent ability to reduce ΔP_ave, while maintaining a notably high PF. This is achieved by shrinking recirculation bubble size within mixing chambers. Therefore, this specific Eddy corner chamfer BFSFO model is highly recommended for use in combustion or heat transfer applications. Frequency increases across baseline, step, and Eddy corner chamfer models occur due to higher velocity return flows inside feedback channels, which helps accelerate jet movement cycles.

title: Analytical study of free and forced vibrations in scale-dependent refined torsional Rao’s non-circular nanobeams
venue: International Journal of Dynamics and Control
abstract: This paper investigates the torsional vibration behavior of non-circular nanobeams using Rao’s refined torsion theory, which incorporates the warping function into all components of the displacement field. In the torsional vibration of non-circular nanobeams, the warping of the cross section leads to the appearance of in-plane strains. Classical torsion theories do not account for all in-plane strain components. To overcome this limitation, Rao’s refined torsion theory considers the Poisson effect in the displacement field, thereby ensuring that all in-plane strains are fully incorporated. The warping function explicitly accounts for these Poisson-induced in-plane deformations, enabling a more accurate and physically consistent description of torsional behavior in non-circular cross sections, such as elliptical and rectangular shapes. For the first time, Rao’s refined theory is used with the nonlocal strain gradient (NSG) framework to capture size-dependent phenomena in the torsional vibration of non-circular nanobeams. The nanobeam is assumed to be subjected to a longitudinal magnetic field and supported by an elastic foundation. Hamilton’s principle is used to derive the governing equations for free and forced torsional vibrations. Natural frequencies are analyzed with respect to key parameters, including length-scale parameters, aspect ratio, magnetic field permeability, and elastic foundation stiffness. The forced vibration response under a harmonic moving torque is also investigated, and the results are compared with those of the classical theory, highlighting the significant roles of warping, size effects, and magnetic fields. The findings provide valuable physical insights for the design of nanoscale torsional devices.

title: Cell-based distributed NiTi-ST damping for dynamic vibration control of hourglass composite lattice sandwich beams
abstract: Hourglass composite lattice sandwich beams (HCLSBs) possess excellent stiffness-to-weight efficiency, yet their dynamic vibration response requires further investigation. This paper establishes a modified Timoshenko beam model with bending-shear coupling for HCLSBs. The vibration response is systematically analyzed by the Galerkin truncation method (GTM) combined with the harmonic balance method (HBM), and the modal characteristics are validated through the finite element analysis and impact hammer experiments on fabricated physical specimens. On this basis, two distributed passive damping schemes based on nitinol steel wire rope (NiTi-ST) are designed and compared, including embedded and cell-based configurations. Vibration experiments demonstrate that both schemes effectively attenuate resonant responses. However, the NiTi-ST cell configuration exhibits superior damping efficiency on a mass-normalized basis. The proposed modeling framework and the distributed damping strategy provide an effective solution for vibration suppression in lightweight lattice structures, holding significant potential for applications in structural dynamics and control engineering, particularly in aerospace component design.

title: Nonlinear transient response analysis of FGM sandwich structures with stepped face sheets
venue: Archives of Civil and Mechanical Engineering
abstract: This paper focuses on sandwich panels with stepped functionally graded material (FGM) layers and initial geometric imperfections, exploring their nonlinear transient behavior when placed on viscoelastic bases and subjected to sinusoidal forces.
